newsitem.title: POLAND: Shy Polish poet apprehensive after Nobel prize.
newsitem.headline: Shy Polish poet apprehensive after Nobel prize.

text.p: Famously shy Polish poet Wislawa Szymborska, taken by surprise at winning this year's Nobel Literature Prize, said on Thursday she was delighted but also apprehensive at being flung into the world literary limelight.

"This is a difficult situation. I am normally a very private person and now I foresee some difficult moments," Szymborska, 73, laughing with excitement, told Reuters by telephone from a hotel for writers in the mountain resort of Zakopane.
"I am very pleased for Polish literature although there are other poets like me in Poland...Tadeusz Rozewicz and Zbigniew Herbert to mention only two," Szymborska said.
She said that although she had been mentioned among the candidates, her selection by the Swedish academy -- which carries a $1.12 million award, had come as a surprise.

Szymborska paid warm tribute to Anders Bodegard, Swedish translator of her poems, which the academy recognised were hard to translate due to their stylistic variety. "If this had been a mediocre translator we would not be talking today," she said.
Asked whether she would now appear more in public and perhaps give lectures abroad, the slight, grey-haired poet said she might be willing to travel but commented: "No, I never give lectures."
